steps.text: The sound of steam.
Heavy gushing.

a.text: 'Not bad, **. A Steam Knight at your age! You're our pride, and the pride of Victoria!'

steps.text: Unintelligible syllables. Is someone calling his name?
But he cannot remember his own name anymore.
Evans? Jones? Wilson? Lynch?
None of them, and all of them.

a.text: 'We vow to defend Victoria unto our last breath.'

steps.text: But why...
Why were his fellows hidden in the shadows behind the outlanders' swords?
His comrades fell, one by one.
In the end, he was the only one left. He was The Last Steam Knight.
He cannot fall here. The Steam Knights must not fall.
Victoria needs him. He must fulfill his duty.
No medicine, no matter. The armor will repair his flesh and blood.
No food, no matter. There are always critters crawling in the darkness.
No light, no matter. The sword gives him all the light he needs.
He is not dead. The Steam Knights are not dead. They continue to defend Victoria.
But...
What is Victoria?
I swore an oath before the King, before the people, before the world.
I stood vigil, night after night, but where lies the light of Victoria that I have sworn fealty to?
Is Victoria its king?
They hanged the king.
Is Victoria Parliament and the nobles?
No maintenance, no supplies, no new members. They sent the Steam Knights into mortal danger time after time, in order to feed their greed.
Is Victoria the people?

The people praise the Steam Knights, honor the Steam Knights, glorify the Steam Knights. They place all their hopes, all their dreams upon the Steam Knights. Nothing can carry hopes that are so contradictory, so complex.
What is Victoria?
Does Victoria only exist in the imagination?
There is still the sword, the Sighs of Kings.
It is the symbol of Victoria, beyond all doubt.
Then it will be his Victoria.
Now, someone wants to defile his Victoria.
This is unacceptable.
He cannot lose his last—

steps.name: 'The Last Steam Knight'
steps.text: (Heavy gushing)

steps.name: 'The Last Steam Knight'
steps.text: 'Victoria.'

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: D-Do you hear, knight?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I cannot command you.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I ask you to allow us to take the sword.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Not because of who I am.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Londinium needs it.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: No, not Londinium.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: The children shivering in orphanages need it. The farmers who lost hearth and home to war need it.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: The workers pouring sweat and blood into their machines need it. The citizens who drink away their helplessness need it.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: The soldiers who step forward to protect their homes need it. Rhodes Island, trying to avert disaster, needs it.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: It is not a storm that it will dispel. It is the fear.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: This is how it must be used.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: It's not your Victoria, knight.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Allow me to pass.
Not Victoria?
Then where is Victoria?
The Steam Knight is filled with confusion and anger.
Where is Victoria?!
What is the Victoria that he served?!

steps.name: 'The Last Steam Knight'
steps.text: (Heavy gushing)

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: He's getting faster!

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: We can't stop him!

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Allerdale!

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Your Highness Alexandrina.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Do you remember the day we met?

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: We should have spoken more. You appeared at the ducal manor, with that sword.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: It was a beautiful afternoon.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: There was music in the garden. The flowers bloomed brightly. People danced and talked about tomorrow. Everything was filled with hope.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: I boasted that I would become a Steam Knight.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: The light shone upon the sword... and upon you.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: They said what happened that afternoon was a miracle.
She was running.
The freshly-trimmed grass made her feet itch. Jim the Gardener laughed by the bushes. Ailshie ran after her, calling for her to slow down.
But she was eager to run towards the freshly-blooming flowers. They were golden, shining under the sun, like the emblem of House Cumberland.
Her father picked her up, sat her on his shoulder. She lifted her tiny palm, and let her touch the lines on the steam armor.
The broken armor stands up.
Her father is gone. She has grown up, and she no longer stands before the armor. She feels the heavy weight of the armor on her shoulder.
Through her visor, she sees a golden lion at the end of the path.

a.text: You will meet Vina again, someday.'

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: It's been hard for me to believe in miracles, after all these years.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Ailshie told me that I don't know who I will be.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: I'm afraid there won't be a 'will be'.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: How old was I? I don't remember. I promised Ailshie that I'd become a Steam Knight and protect everyone.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: At least, I have the chance to face a Steam Knight now.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: I hear you, Vina. There's no such thing as fate or destiny.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Not for House Cumberland, not for the dukes.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: To hell with destiny. I'm tired.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Tired of playing a noble, playing a leader, playing a friend.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: You're the leader of the Self-Salvation Corps because they trust you.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: You're my friend because I say you are.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Hah. That's enough, Vina.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Let's put an end to the fable.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Tell Morgan to cast me in a better light in her memoir, Dagda.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Use more refined words, at least.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: What's going on?

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: The wind...
A gust of wind blows them outside.
One solemn face falls after another, as the statues of the kings collapse, one by one.
The rubble separates them from the Steam Knight... and someone else.
Siege immediately reacts.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Allerdale!

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Forgive me...
Her lips move slightly.
Siege knows Allerdale called to her.
Was it 'Vina'? Or 'Your Highness'?
Siege does not know.
She may never know.
The sound is drowned by the rubble.
The door is shut.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Alright, come now, my nightmare...

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: My hope.

steps.name: 'The Last Steam Knight'
steps.text: (Heavy gushing)
One scene floats to the surface of the Steam Knight's tumultuous memories.
A girl sheds tears for him before he stands up.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Pah—

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Son of a—

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: There's nowhere to run!

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Last smoke grenade. We still have a chance.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: You've done enough, mercenary.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Surrender, and they might let you live.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: No way. How many more years would I have to work?
Enough.
End this.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Were you the ones manipulating Allerdale?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: No, it's not you. The cowardly dukes wouldn't dare show their faces here.
Allerdale has failed. Alexandrina has the Sighs of Kings.
What a boring conclusion.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: You know what?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: You will do.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: You will pay for all that you've done!

steps.name: Tyrant
steps.text: Stop, traitor!

steps.name: Knight
steps.text: Nothing can stop me. You must pay for your crimes.

steps.name: Tyrant
steps.text: You will die with me!

steps.name: Knight
steps.text: The death of the flesh does not daunt me. Countless eyes will bear witness.

steps.name: Knight
steps.text: Brave children, you will carry the torch.

steps.name: Knight
steps.text: You will remember my virtues, and take this hard-earned peace into tomorrow.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: The end.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: That was wonderful, Lady Golding. A great success.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: The product of a year of everyone's hard work.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: I wish we were in more peaceful times. That way, Heidi could have been here to see it.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: It's times like these that we need a play like this.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Look how happy the kids are—

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Hey, Leo! Don't run with the props!

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: Get back here!

steps.name: Innocent Child
steps.text: Get back here!

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: Run, run! I'll come for you! Great Victoria will come for you!

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: Hie over the valleys and over the rivers, rumble-ye-rumble...

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: Crush them! Squeeze the blood from them!

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: Die! You'll all die! I'll catch you and kill you!

steps.name: Innocent Child
steps.text: Squeeze it out!

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: Surrender, Sarkaz!

steps.name: Innocent Child
steps.text: Surrender!

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: Or not, because I'll catch you!

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Stop! You're ruining Lady Golding's handmade 'steam armor'!

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: They...

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Don't be angry, Lady Golding. They're just playing a game.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: A game...?

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Yes. The play has ended.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: 'Squeeze the blood from them'?

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: It's... the Sarkaz...
She sees before her eyes the red that filled the bookstore.
She does not even have the strength to vomit.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: It's normal.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: We're in a war, after all.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: The Sarkaz have been arresting people left and right, often in violent ways. The children see them, and emulate their behavior.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Do you know, Molly...?

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Many remnants of Gaul harbor fear of the Steam Knights.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Those who were part of the war will never forget the sound of steam gushing outside their window that night.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: But I had hoped that the Steam Knights would be more than just a weapon of death to the children.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: I had hoped that there would be beautiful hope in their hearts when they play the Steam Knight.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: I thought this was a war I could win.
Golding's gaze follows the children.
The foam-made steam armor falls to the ground. She tries to pick it up, but pulls back sharply, as though she's been burned.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: I thought I was teaching the children...

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Now, I realize that they were the ones teaching me a lesson.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: This, here, is the ending. The true ending.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Before the wheels of time...

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: What we do may be utterly meaningless.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: The lessons of the books are distant, blurred.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: But no one can avoid being shaped by the times.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: If they belong to blood, violence and war...

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Then, our children will belong to blood, violence and war.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: This is unavoidable.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: What... what should I...

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: How could I dream of fighting it?
